presentation.label: CC Assignment Names
presentation.summary: Give each MIDI CC assignment a label of up to five characters. Labels appear on CC VALUE and follow native pattern and project operations.
presentation.overview: Give each MIDI CC assignment a label of up to five characters. Labels appear on CC VALUE and follow native pattern and project operations.
highlights: Open the native name editor for that CC VALUE slot.
Move the text cursor and change a character in the name editor.
Accept the name / cancel the edit.
usage: Select MIDI A with TRK + trig 9. Set the desired CC number on CC SELECT, then press FLTR for CC VALUE.
Hold FUNC and press and hold the encoder for the assignment you want to name.
Use LEFT/RIGHT to select a character and UP/DOWN to change it. Enter a short name such as CUTO.
Press YES to accept, or NO to cancel. The label appears below that assignment; turning its encoder still sends the assigned CC.

access.location: MIDI track CC VALUE page; hold FUNC and the assignment encoder
steps: Select MIDI A with TRK + trig 9. Set the desired CC number on CC SELECT, then press FLTR for CC VALUE.

controls.name: FUNC + hold A–H
controls.doc: Open the native name editor for that CC VALUE slot.

controls.name: LEFT/RIGHT and UP/DOWN
controls.doc: Move the text cursor and change a character in the name editor.

controls.name: YES / NO
controls.doc: Accept the name / cancel the edit.

controls.name: Short FUNC + encoder press
controls.doc: Retains the native CC-enable toggle; hold longer to rename.

limitations: Labels are limited to five characters.
Labels do not change CC numbers or MIDI values.
Stock firmware can discard the added name data when saving projects.

load.display: Adds under 0.1% of an audio block over stock, average and worst case (emulator)
load.conditions: Emulator: OS 1.53 on Core 2.1, 8 audio tracks triggering a full-scale sample and 8 MIDI tracks a note on every step at 120 BPM, 3,000 audio blocks timed with the MCF5441x instruction-timing model at 250 MHz, zero-wait memory. Module workload: no audio-path feature (CC names are UI only). Stock: 59.1% average, 61.8% worst block. All six mods together: 73.2% worst block on 1.53, 73.3% on 1.54. Not a hardware measurement.

hardware.summary: sumedho reports the Core 2.1 all-mods builds fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours in total, including project save and reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14): “ok fully tested on hardware and working”.
limitations: Duration is the reporter’s range (1–2 hours) for the combined session across both OS releases; recorded as 90 minutes.
Individual test outcomes were not itemized; standalone (single-mod) hardware coverage is not claimed.
Tested SysEx: 1.53 23503ca42478c1644dea5fd296893f628eafb6662d2ce5e291bfc591f045ae4e, 1.54 257144e4a584172e470c3dde83d7ccda636eeb195b4e5ff0492b3ebc8bdfaba2; firmware was not read back from the device.

tests.summary: Runs on Core 2.1. Emulator regressions on OS 1.53 and 1.54, an emulator CPU-load comparison with stock, and Modwerk source-build parity with the native build are in TESTING.md. sumedho reports this Core 2.1 build fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours including project save/reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14).
